contracts.description: loom's knowledge wing: cited entity pages in a SQLite store separate from memory, with a sourced/provisional epistemic gate, deterministic LIKE recall that never surfaces archived pages, an archive/restore/supersede/move/merge/purge/verify lifecycle that is destruction-averse (archive-first purge, body-immutable verify, auto-snapshotted revisions, surviving supersession pointers), and the knowledge-vs-memory boundary. Observed in src/server.ts, src/tools/knowledge-*.ts, and src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts of loom (github.com/jbarket/loom), v0.4 line.

exclusions: The embedding/vector machinery: knowledge deliberately uses no embeddings (plain SQLite LIKE) — the non-deterministic ranking that the memory wing's recall projects is simply absent here, not modeled.

Wall-clock and id generation: every write/move/merge/verify/archive stamps new Date() and creates randomUUID()s; these timestamps and ids are not observable in a pure return-value fixture and bind as prose (the inspection-verified residue class).
MCP transport, CLI, and store-file location (the context dir, WAL pragmas, user_version) are binding surface; only the command/result values and the store's logical schema are contract.
goals: Record loom's knowledge-wing contract — the entity-page store distinct from episodic memory: cited, sourced/provisional epistemics, deterministic LIKE retrieval (no embeddings), the archive/supersede/move/merge/purge/verify/history lifecycle, and the boundaries it refuses to cross. Read out of the loomai codebase (github.com/jbarket/loom, v0.4 line), nothing authored.

Knowledge recall is deterministic (LIKE over title/body/domain), so its filter/order is fixtured directly — the projection device the memory wing needs for its vector ranking is absent here. Side-effects (timestamps, access stamping, revision snapshots) are the unfixturable facets, inspection-verified.
spec.name: loom-knowledge

spec.body: Every knowledge_write requires at least one citation (server.ts:384-430; handler knowledge-write.ts:52-58) — there is no uncited knowledge. A page's sourcing is derived, not declared: a page whose every citation is of source_kind 'conversation' (or which somehow has none) is filed sourcing='provisional'; any non-conversation citation (web, loom_memory) makes it 'sourced' (determineSourcing, knowledge-write.ts:40-46). provisional is loom saying "the sole support is our own talk" — and knowledge_maintain's misfile audit flags such pages as candidate memories. Bodies are capped at 64 KB and citation excerpts at 4 KB (sqlite-knowledge.ts:1074-1090); over-cap writes throw.
spec.title: Cited and sourced — the epistemic gate

spec.evidence: src ref: src/tools/knowledge-write.ts:52-58 (>=1 citation required) and src/server.ts:384-430 (write registration); body/excerpt caps at src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts:1074-1090.

spec.body: knowledge_recall has two paths. By slug (precedence): an active page returns full and stamps access; an ARCHIVED page returns a restore hint and is NOT stamped; a missing slug returns a not-found message (knowledge-recall.ts:106-121). By query: a whitespace-tokenized LIKE search where every token must match title OR body OR domain (AND across tokens, no token-length filter), the domain filter is prefix-inclusive (domain = ? OR domain LIKE ?/%), ordered hit_count DESC, updated DESC, created DESC (or verified_at ASC NULLS FIRST when sort_by_verified), and ALWAYS excludes archived (excludeStatus 'archived' passed unconditionally) — sqlite-knowledge.ts queryPages:266-334, recall handler:123-176. There are NO embeddings and no cosine ranking anywhere in the knowledge wing (it never loads sqlite-vec) — recall is a pure, fixturable function of the page set and the query, the deterministic contrast with the memory wing's vector recall. detail 'full' returns whole pages and stamps last_accessed+hit_count; detail 'index' returns compact entries and does not stamp; full output is size-guarded at 24,000 chars, degrading overflow to index entries (first page always shown full).
spec.title: Recall is deterministic LIKE — archived pages never surface

spec.evidence: src ref: src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts queryPages:266-334 (token AND match over title/body/domain, prefix-inclusive domain, order hit_count/updated/created, excludeStatus archived); recall handler src/tools/knowledge-recall.ts:123-176; no sqlite-vec in the knowledge backend (factory src/backends/index.ts:81-86).
spec.gherkin:
Given a set of pages and a multi-token query
When knowledge_recall runs
Then it returns exactly the active pages where every token LIKE-matches title, body, or domain (AND across tokens), ordered by hit_count then updated then created, excluding every archived page — a pure deterministic function of the pages and query, with no embedding or cosine ranking

Given recall by an exact slug for an active page and for an archived page
When each runs
Then the active page returns in full and is access-stamped, while the archived page returns a restore hint and is NOT stamped — archived pages surface only as a pointer to restore
spec.triggeringEvent: loom brownfield excavation (felag, the loom-knowledge dig)

spec.body: A page's lifecycle axis is status active|archived, orthogonal to the sourced|provisional epistemic axis. archive sets status='archived' with an optional tombstone_note and bumps updated; archiving a missing or already-archived page is an idempotent no-op reporting archived=false (sqlite-knowledge.ts archivePage:336-357). restore is the exact mirror: it returns an archived page to active and CLEARS the tombstone, else restored=false (restorePage:359-380). supersede is a 1:1 dedup pointer: both slugs must exist (it rejects on a missing old or new, and the handler rejects old==new), and if old is already archived it early-returns archived=false writing nothing; otherwise, in one transaction, it archives old with a tombstone "Superseded by <new>" and inserts a supersessions(old_slug, new_slug, note) row (supersedePage:382-432). supersession rows are plain TEXT with no foreign key — they are the historical trail and survive purge and hard-delete.
spec.title: Archive, restore, supersede — status and the pointer trail

spec.evidence: src ref: src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts archivePage:336-357 (status archived + tombstone + updated; missing/already -> archived false) and restorePage:359-380 (archived -> active, tombstone NULL; else restored false).
spec.gherkin:
Given an active page, then archive, then restore
When each runs
Then archive sets status archived with the tombstone note and reports archived true; a second archive is an idempotent no-op (archived false); restore returns it to active and CLEARS the tombstone (restored true); restoring a non-archived page is restored false
spec.triggeringEvent: loom brownfield excavation (felag, the loom-knowledge dig)

spec.evidence: src ref: src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts supersedePage:382-432 (reject missing 390-400; old-archived early return 402-404 before the tx; tx archives old + inserts supersessions 413-420); handler old==new reject src/tools/knowledge-supersede.ts:25-27; supersessions schema (no FK) 1036-1042.
spec.gherkin:
Given supersede with a missing old or new slug, with old equal to new, with old already archived, and with two valid distinct active pages
When each runs
Then missing endpoints reject, old==new rejects, an already-archived old early-returns archived false writing NO supersession row, and the valid case archives old with a 'Superseded by <new>' tombstone and records a supersessions(old,new) pointer that has no foreign key
spec.triggeringEvent: loom brownfield excavation (felag, the loom-knowledge dig)

spec.body: knowledge_move re-keys a page (same uuid, citations, verification preserved) in three mutually-selected modes: a domain-prefix batch, a slug-list batch (rolls the whole transaction back if any slug is missing), and a single-page rename of slug and/or domain. A single move that collides with an existing slug is REJECTED and redirected to knowledge_merge — never a silent overwrite — and a slug rename writes a supersessions pointer 'slug rename via knowledge_move' unless leave_pointer is false (movePage:434-567). knowledge_merge consolidates N sources into one target: it rejects an empty source set, a source equal to the target, a missing target, or any missing source; per source it dedups citations identical to the target's by the (claim, source_kind, locator, excerpt) tuple and re-parents the rest to the target, sets the target's verified_at to the MAX across all merged pages, archives each source with a "Merged into <target>" tombstone and a supersession pointer, optionally appends loser bodies under markers, and optionally hard-deletes the losers (their citations cascade, their supersession pointers survive) — mergePages:569-713.
spec.title: Move and merge — re-key and consolidate, never silently clobber

spec.evidence: src ref: src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts movePage:434-567 (collision reject->merge 514-525; slug-list rollback on missing 480-482; rename writes pointer 537-542 default leave_pointer true 529).

Given a single-page move whose new slug collides with an existing page, a slug-list move with one missing slug, and a clean single-page rename
When each runs
Then the collision is rejected and redirected to knowledge_merge (never a silent overwrite), the missing-slug batch rolls back whole, and the clean rename preserves the uuid and citations and writes a 'slug rename via knowledge_move' supersession pointer unless leave_pointer is false

Given merge with an empty source set, a source equal to the target, and two real sources into a target
When each runs
Then the empty set and the self-merge reject, and the real merge re-parents each source's citations to the target after dropping those identical to the target's by (claim, source_kind, locator, excerpt), sets the target verified_at to the MAX across all merged pages, archives each source with a 'Merged into <target>' tombstone and a supersession pointer, and on hard_delete deletes the losers while their supersession pointers survive
spec.triggeringEvent: loom brownfield excavation (felag, the loom-knowledge dig)

spec.body: knowledge_verify stamps verified_at (and optional freshness_anchor) WITHOUT touching the body — the primitive added after a 2026-06-01 incident where verifying through knowledge_write stomped 13 bodies. It accepts exactly one of slug|slugs (XOR), batch mode forbids note and freshness_anchor, it rejects an archived page and whole-batch-rejects any unknown slug, a single-page note is APPENDED as a '## Verification — <date>' section (never a replace), and the pure stamp deliberately does NOT bump updated while a note does (verifyPages:762-836). knowledge_purge hard-deletes archived pages and cascades their citations, but only with confirm: literal true, and only after an archive-first guard validates ALL slugs before any mutation — any missing or any still-ACTIVE page rejects the whole batch with no deletion; supersession pointers survive the purge (purgePages:715-760). knowledge_maintain is a READ-ONLY audit (no mutation): over active pages it reports expansion candidates (hit_count >= threshold AND body shorter than a thin-body floor), cold pages (never accessed or last_accessed older than coldDays), and misfiled pages (provisional or conversation-only) — knowledge-maintain.ts.
spec.title: Verify, purge, maintain — body-immutable, archive-first, read-only

spec.body: Replace-writes and restores auto-snapshot the displaced body into page_revisions (op 'write-replace' / 'history-restore'), capped at 10 revisions per page (sqlite-knowledge.ts:48, 103-105, 919-936). knowledge_history is the recovery surface: list returns revision metadata newest-first; read returns a snapshot body by revision_id; restore puts a snapshot's body back AND snapshots the currently-displaced body first, so restore is never destructive, validating that the page and revision exist and that the revision belongs to that page (restoreRevision:872-916). Body loss is always recoverable for the last 10 revisions.
spec.title: History — every body change is recoverable

spec.evidence: src ref: src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts write-replace snapshot 103-105 (MAX_REVISIONS_PER_PAGE 10, line 48); listRevisions 838-852 (id DESC); restoreRevision:872-916 (snapshot displaced first 896-904; revision-belongs-to-page check 890-894).
spec.gherkin:
Given a page replace-written twice (snapshotting the prior body) and then a history restore of an old revision
When history list/read/restore run
Then list returns the revisions newest-first, restore puts the chosen snapshot's body back AND snapshots the currently-displaced body first so nothing is lost, and a restore of a revision that does not belong to the page is rejected
spec.triggeringEvent: loom brownfield excavation (felag, the loom-knowledge dig)

spec.body: The filing test is stated verbatim in the tool surface: "Knowledge is true independent of Jonathan — if it is about Jonathan or our work, store it in memory instead" (server.ts:389-390). Knowledge pages are world-facts about entities; facts about the user, the work, or the agent belong in the memory wing. The two wings are SEPARATE databases (knowledge.db vs memories.db), hard-isolated by a path/inode co-location assertion that throws (config.ts:90-99). The knowledge surface deliberately refuses: uncited knowledge (write needs a citation), hard-deletion of active pages (purge is archive-first), verification that mutates a body (verify is body-immutable), silent overwrite on slug collision (move redirects to merge), and loss of the supersession trail (pointers have no FK and survive deletion).
spec.title: What knowledge is, and what loom refuses

spec.evidence: src ref: src/server.ts:389-390 (knowledge_write desc: 'Knowledge is true independent of Jonathan — if it is about Jonathan or our work, store it in memory instead'); separate-db isolation src/config.ts:90-99; provisional->candidate-memory in src/tools/knowledge-maintain.ts:109-125.
spec.item: A fact true independently of Jonathan — a world-fact about some entity — belongs in the knowledge wing; a fact about Jonathan, the work, or the agent itself belongs in episodic memory. The two wings are SEPARATE, hard-isolated databases. Knowledge stores cited entity pages; memory stores categorized episodic facts. A page whose only support is conversation is provisional and is a candidate to be re-filed as a memory.
spec.triggeringEvent: loom brownfield excavation (felag, the loom-knowledge dig)

spec.evidence: src ref: write citation req knowledge-write.ts:52-58; purge archive-first src/backends/sqlite-knowledge.ts:738-742 + confirm src/server.ts:635; verify body-immutable verifyPages:762-836; move->merge collision 514-525; body/excerpt caps 1074-1090; supersessions no-FK survival 1036-1042.
spec.item: The knowledge surface refuses, on purpose: uncited knowledge (write requires a citation), hard-deletion of an active page (purge is archive-first + confirm), verification that mutates a body (verify is body-immutable), silent overwrite on a slug collision (move redirects to merge), body bloat (64 KB body / 4 KB excerpt caps), and loss of the supersession trail (pointers have no foreign key and survive every deletion). Each refusal is a drawn boundary, not an accident.
spec.triggeringEvent: loom brownfield excavation (felag, the loom-knowledge dig)

spec.description: archive flips active->archived with a tombstone (idempotent on re-archive); restore returns to active and clears the tombstone.
A write with no citations is rejected; a write with at least one citation is accepted — there is no uncited knowledge.
Replace-writes snapshot the displaced body; restore puts an old body back and snapshots the current one first (never destructive); a foreign revision is rejected.
merge rejects empty/self; a real merge re-parents citations (dedup vs target), takes MAX verified_at, archives losers with pointers; hard delete keeps the pointers.
A colliding move is rejected toward merge; a clean rename preserves uuid and writes a rename pointer.
purge needs confirm:true and is archive-first: any active or unknown slug rejects the whole batch; an all-archived confirmed batch deletes while pointers survive.
A query never surfaces an archived page even when it matches.
By-slug recall of an active page returns it in full and stamps access.
By-slug recall of an archived page returns a restore hint and does NOT stamp.
Multi-token query: every token must LIKE-match title/body/domain (AND); results ordered hit_count, updated, created.
hard-deleting an active page is refused (purge is archive-first).
knowledge with no citation is refused.

spec.description: All citations of kind conversation (or none) -> provisional: the sole support is our own talk.
A single loom_memory citation -> sourced (any non-conversation kind suffices).
A mix containing a web citation -> sourced.
supersede rejects missing endpoints and self; an already-archived old writes no pointer; the valid case archives old + records a surviving pointer.
verify stamps verified_at without touching the body, rejects archived and unknown, and a pure stamp does not bump updated while a note does.
